title: Varieties with dominant rational maps are equivalent to finitely generated field extensions
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section on function fields of varieties
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: The theorem asserts an equivalence between two categories: varieties over k with dominant rational maps, and finitely generated field extensions K/k (statement lines 166-168). The proof has to do two different jobs, and the difficulty is in seeing that they suffice: full faithfulness comes from reading a dominant rational map as the induced map of function fields k(Y) -> k(X) at the generic points and inverting it with the cited lemma on rational maps of finite presentation, while the essential image needs the separate observation that a finitely generated extension is the fraction field of a finite type k-algebra A, so that Spec(A) is a variety having K as its function field (proof lines 172-192). Neither direction is a computation; both are structural, which is why the claim is H2 and not lower.
